topics.topic_label: Agent execution control (containment stopped being an argument and became an incident log - and the commercial answer landed on the same calendar page: Snowflake and Databricks both ship control planes that enforce identity, policy and audit at the tool-call level rather than at the API edge; a 40k-run study finds human reviewers miss one dangerous agent command in three, which removes human-in-the-loop as a primary control; Resourced Authority models who can actually stop a running agent as mechanism design)

EU AI Act (the AI Office's GPAI enforcement powers went live 2 August with fines to EUR 15M or 3% of global turnover, and five separate Pulse pieces in one day work the same seam - Article 14 oversight is a legal specification rather than a slogan, Article 50 binds deployers regardless of risk class, existing observability traces already satisfy much of the logging duty, and autonomy does not move responsibility from the company to the agent)

Agent execution control (across 40k plays and 409k decisions humans approved roughly a third of genuinely risky agent commands AFTER an explicit warning — "click yes to proceed" was never a security mechanism, it is a CYA click-through; ServiceNow ships a Veza-backed real-time kill switch for agents operating beyond their permissions; a six-check human-approval control set is argued against three named same-week failures)

EU AI Act (enforcement operative since 2 August — the AI Office can demand technical documentation from GPAI providers, evaluate models, require risk mitigations and levy fines up to €15M or 3% of global turnover, while the Digital Omnibus deferred high-risk obligations to Dec 2027 / Aug 2028 but left prohibitions and transparency duties on the original date; the underdiscussed vector is that any third party, competitors included, can file a complaint a national authority is then obliged to act on)
